item.title: Pokemon GO Gets Crocs Collaboration With Free Gift Code
item.description:
Pokemon GO has announced a new collaboration with Crocs, and players can now redeem a free code for a special avatar item. Pokemon GO frequently features collaborations meant to build hype for other products and announcements. Past collaborations have connected directly with new video games like Pokemon Pokopia and Detective Pikachu Returns , while others have helped to draw attention to products like LEGO sets, and even shows like Pokemon Concierge .

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Earlier this year, Crocs revealed a trio of Pokemon shoe designs. Pikachu and Gengar each received their own pair of Classic Clogs, while Jigglypuff uses a Platform Clog design. The top of each shoe features that Pokemon's head, while the sides feature accents specific to that character. For example, the Pikachu Classic Clogs have lightning bolts on the sides, while the Jigglypuff shoes have music notes.

Pokemon Legends: Z-A Giving Away Two Shiny Legendary Pokemon For a Limited Time

Pokemon Legends: Z-A announces a new distribution event, allowing players the chance to obtain the Shiny versions of two Legendary Pokemon.

By Marc Deschamps

Crocs Avatar Items Come to Pokemon GO

Developer Scopely Explore has revealed that the new footwear designs from Crocs are being added to Pokemon GO , which means that players will be able to wear replicas of the Pikachu, Gengar, and Jigglypuff designs in the game. Pokemon GO players even have a code to redeem, which will grant them one of the avatar items for free. The code POKEMONGOxCROCSxELECTRIFYING automatically unlocks the Pikachu Classic Clogs, offering a new customization option without the need to spend any PokeCoins. The code isn't set to expire until December 31, 2027, so players have quite some time to take advantage of the offer.

The Jigglypuff and Gengar avatar items will be a bit tougher for players to obtain. Rather than offering them through Pokemon GO 's PokeCoin in-game currency, codes for the clogs will be given out to those who purchase the real-world versions. At this time, this seems to be the only way players can get the Gengar and Jigglypuff designs in the game. However, it appears that the codes are not unique, and some generous Pokemon fans are already sharing the codes online.

Reception to the giveaway has been largely positive. The Crocs offer a unique option that helps set them apart from other avatar options, and they should be a big hit for fans of those three Pokemon, specifically. While some players don't like the frequent collaborations in Pokemon GO , it's tough to complain too much about free avatar items. Between Remote Raid passes, Link Charges, and event tickets, it's easy to spend a lot of money on Pokemon GO . Free avatar items help soften the blow, allowing players to customize their in-game Trainer without blowing through all of their PokeCoins.

Pokemon GO 's current Twilight Trails season will soon come to an end, and a new one is set to begin on December 1. Scopely Explore has not revealed what the new theme will be, though a schedule for Pokemon GO 's next Community Days and other major events has already been revealed. The new season should bring more Pokemon to catch, more Mega Evolutions, and a lot more avatar items to be obtained in the shop.

item.title: New 95% Positive Steam Roguelike Has an Unusual Answer to Slay the Spire's Formula
item.description:
It's interesting how roguelike deckbuilders have become increasingly popular, and it's no secret that Slay the Spire has set the standard with their established, resource-driven formula. I think that the appeal comes from a balance between three main features: deck construction, calculated risks, and the ability to anticipate enemy attacks before committing to a turn. Now, a new contender is offering a different approach to that familiar formula. Novus Orbis , which officially left Steam Early Access on November 13, has already earned a 95% Positive rating on Steam.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

It's a compelling twist on the genre: rather than allowing players to rely entirely on predictable enemy intentions, opponents can change their behavior during the player’s turn, forcing them to reconsider their strategies on the fly. I think it raises the question of whether less predictable combat can create deeper strategic possibilities, without just adding more randomness. Its 1.0 release is seemingly off to a great start, so using Slay the Spire as a familiar benchmark offers a way to explore what Novus Orbis does differently.

Slay the Spire 2: Tips and Tricks for Beginners

Become a master of the Spire with these helpful suggestions.

By Matt Vatankhah

Novus Orbit Has a Different Answer to Slay the Spire's Predictable Combat

I think that the main reason Slay the Spire remains such an influential roguelike deckbuilder is how much information it gives players before they make their moves. This means that enemy intentions are clearly telegraphed, so the player is already informed if the opponent plans to attack, defend, or use a special ability on their next turn. Yes, it might seem like a simple design choice, but it has a considerable impact on how each encounter plays out without relying on mere guesswork. Weighing up threats and deciding how best to use your available energy and cards is part of the fun, and really requires players to think and plan properly.

Wishlist Today

I don't think that this predictability doesn't necessarily make combat easy. In fact, it often makes difficult encounters a great deal more satisfying because players have the information they need to make informed decisions (even when they don’t have an ideal hand). Do I spend my energy defending against an incoming attack, or take the opportunity to deal enough damage to eliminate an enemy first? These well-thought decisions lay at the heart of Slay the Spire 's strategic appeal, but I think that’s where Novus Orbis can take the opportunity to offer an even more dynamic approach.

Its 1.0 release is seemingly off to a great start, so using Slay the Spire as a familiar benchmark offers a way to explore what Novus Orbis does differently.

Here sits the biggest difference between Novus Orbis and Slay the Spire : its Countdown system, which makes enemy intentions an active part of every turn. It's not something players can just prepare for beforehand, basically. Each enemy has a countdown towards its next action, and every card played advances that countdown by one step. Ending a turn advances it by another two steps, meaning opponents can attack before players have even finished using their available cards. I do feel it creates a refreshing dilemma, as players are forced to consider interrupting their plans to deal with an approaching threat.

Novus Orbis also features three playable classes, more than 330 unique cards, 119 Blessings that provide powerful upgrades, and 10 pets that can attack, heal, or support players throughout combat. There is even an Endless Mode for players who want to push their builds beyond a standard run.

The Countdown system is actually only one part of what Novis Orbis brings to the roguelike deckbuilding table. There's also its combo-based card system in which every card has a cost and combo value. Playing cards in the right sequence allows players to unlock their full potential and create opportunities for powerful chains of attacks and abilities. It's definitely a system that encourages experimentation, and an alternative to just building the strongest deck possible and relying on it throughout a run.

Novus Orbis Shows There's Still Room to Experiment With Deckbuilders

With its November 13 1.0 release, Novus Orbis demonstrates how changing the timing of enemy responses can introduce a massive impact and entirely new kind of strategic challenge—without fully abandoning the importance of careful planning that is integral to deckbuilding. For Slay the Spire , giving players the information they need to make calculated decisions creates a satisfying balance between preparation and improvisations. But that doesn’t mean the formula cannot benefit from experimentation.

New 95% Positive Steam Roguelike Has an Unusual Answer to Slay the Spire's Formula
New RPG on Steam is Path of Exile Meets Slay the Spire
Xbox Game Pass Losing One of Its Oldest Games and 7 Other Titles Tomorrow
Brand New Strategy Game on Steam is Slay the Spire Meets Candy Crush with Stanley Parable Writing

I think that whether its Countdown system will appeal to everyone is another matter here. Some players prefer the reassuring predictability of Slay the Spire , especially when building elaborate decks and planning several moves ahead. However, others may appreciate the chance to adapt their combinations as encounters unfold. Either way, Novus Orbis makes a compelling case for looking beyond the genre’s established conventions. Its strong, early Steam reception is certainly an encouraging start, so I'm interested to see if its unusual approach can help it cement a lasting place alongside the deckbuilders that inspired its comparison.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Might Just Be Hiding Its Biggest Surprise in Plain Sight
item.description:
With Grand Theft Auto 6 having been anticipated for 13 long years, and the community having endured multiple delays in the final stretch to launch, it’s almost surreal that Rockstar’s hugely anticipated game is almost here. Naturally, with the open-world crime game so close, hype is reaching new levels. Gamers are watching pre-download streams, calling off work, and speculating about all kinds of theories from classics like “Jason is a cop” to a more recent belief that GTA 6 will be hiding another playable map.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Opinions differ on the location that will serve as the additional map that takes players beyond Leonida—some feel it’ll be Liberty City, others think Gloriana— but frankly, there’s a good deal of evidence for both. Regarding Grand Theft Auto 4’s beloved, New York-inspired locale, clothing from Liberty City has appeared in recent footage, the protagonist Lucia grew up in the city, and a character resembling Tony Prince (AKA Gay Tony) has been shown in a new TV spot. As for the state bordering Leonida, Gloriana obviously has its location working in its favor. Beyond that, there are license plates, apparel, and Boobie’s yacht, which is registered in Gloriana to consider, and many other nods. It feels like there’s plenty of smoke to the fire, especially with Rockstar refusing to show the actual world map ahead of launch, but perhaps it's just world-building. If a secondary location is really going to be featured in GTA 6 , then there are a few ways it could appear.

GTA 6 Officially Confirms Disgusting New Gameplay Feature

Rockstar Games releases new Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay footage that confirms a particularly gross gameplay feature.

By Dalton Cooper

Could GTA 6 Also Feature a Return to Liberty City or Another Map?

Option 1: A ‘Hidden’ Part of the Open World

The simplest way that Rockstar can handle a hidden location would be to work it into the story mode of GTA 6 . In the case of Liberty City, it’s not out of the realm of possibility for the series’ New York stand-in to be featured in a specific chapter of the campaign. Perhaps Lucia’s backstory of growing up in Liberty City and fighting for her family: an act that led to her prison sentence. She learned how to fistfight from her father, after all, so seeing her interact with him and her mother in Liberty City could give the town a narrative purpose beyond being a trip down memory lane.

It’s no secret that Rockstar Games has been inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2 when crafting GTA 6 , as everything from the increased level of detail to the shift toward realism instead of arcadey action can be traced back to that title. Similar menus, safehouses that function like camps, combat focus in place of Deadeye, and body changes are even more examples of similarities. It’s not too outrageous to think, then, that Liberty City could be its own version of Guarma from Red Dead 2 , taking up a few hours of the story mode and offering players a change in scenery. An upscaled version of Liberty City would be easy to hide if it were a separate map players travel to, and with Guarma originally intended to be bigger, Rockstar clearly has interest in going all out with any additional areas in its games, something that makes a second city feel possible for GTA 6 .

As for Gloriana, the fictional equivalent of Georgia being described as Leonida’s border state within Grand Theft Auto lore makes it a natural fit for a “secret city,” as one map could theoretically contain both Leonida and parts of Gloriana in the exact same landmass. Players have already theorized that the northernmost and southernmost sections of the leaked map mock-ups contain interesting surprises, as Rockstar has shown absolutely nothing from these areas yet in the promotional materials thus far. Perhaps there’s simply nothing major to see in these stretches of land, but at the same time, maybe the top of the map extends into another state. All the mountain areas could be a barrier to Gloriana, with two states and major cities offered in the same world as opposed to just Leonida.

Option 2: A DLC Location

Another possibility is that players finally get another single-player DLC from Rockstar Games. While players adored expansions like the original Red Dead Redemption ’s Undead Nightmare and GTA 4 ’s offerings like Ballad of Gay Tony and Lost and the Damned, Rockstar has moved away from this form of content in favor of supporting the more profitable online multiplayer modes. GTA 5, for instance, reportedly had its single-player DLC scrapped. However, with GTA 6 currently being billed as a single-player game, there is a possible window to properly support the game’s single-player offering long-term. Rockstar could fill the void between GTA 6 and the new iteration of GTA Online by dropping a single-player expansion in 2027 or 2028, either taking players to Liberty City or Gloriana. Of all options, though, single-player DLC does feel the least likely to support the fan theory.

Obviously, any cities created for GTA 6 could be repurposed for GTA Online, killing two birds with one stone and making the highly anticipated multiplayer mode even deeper.

Option 3: A Part of GTA Online

The final pathway to a destination beyond Leonida is GTA Online , which is practically guaranteed to get support for years after it debuts. Alongside rumors of built-in role-play features and a Roblox -style “everything game” approach with tons of user-made content, a Fortnite-like evolving map has been a point of speculation. Whether this actually comes to fruition is entirely up in the air, but if the next version of GTA Online is expected to last anywhere as long as the previous one, then it’s easy to imagine a world where it offers players multiple maps to explore, or at least one huge connected one. While Liberty City would have to be a separate map for players to access—perhaps it could be “connected” via a plane trip—the GTA 6 Online map being expanded via areas based in Leonida’s border state is as realistic as it is exciting.

Obviously, Grand Theft Auto 6 players shouldn’t count their chickens before they hatch. Many had hypothesized that GTA 5 would offer more than Los Santos, but it never did. Perhaps the license plates, clothing, and connective tissue between Liberty City and Lucia’s backstory are just a bit of worldbuilding and some fun homages on Rockstar’s past. Still, there are a lot of references showing up in promotional material, with so many mentions of Liberty City and Gloriana that it would almost be surprising if they weren’t included in some way. Fortunately, players won’t have to wait long to find out if their theories are correct.

item.title: The Complete Xbox Game Pass Crossplay List: Every Game (November 2026)
item.description:
Updated on November 16, 2026, by Mark Sammut:

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover
  • The following crossplay games were added in November 2026 (so far): Scramble Knights Online, Void/Breaker, Pit of Goblin, Football Manager 27, Firefighting Simulator: Ignite, Gravhounds, and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando.
  • The following crossplay games left Game Pass in the last month: Deep Rock Galactic, Wartales, Wildgate, Football Manager 26, Police Simulator: Patrol Officers, and Relic Hunters Legend.

Ups and downs aside, Xbox Game Pass continues to be the best deal in console gaming, and a big part of that is its range of options. There is something for everybody, and that includes Xbox Series owners who want to play with their PS5 friends. While not heavily promoted, plenty of cross-platform games are on Game Pass , and new ones tend to be added each and every month. As far as I know, Xbox doesn't let you search by crossplay support, so finding out which games include the feature can be somewhat annoying.

I'm hoping to simplify the process by listing all the Game Pass games that support crossplay. Honestly, I would like to have this information readily available, and sometimes you just have to do the work yourself. Cross-platform should be supported by all modern multiplayer games, not just for us but also for them. When done right, it only extends an online scene's lifespan.

I've tried to be as thorough as possible, but a few things might have slipped by. Still, this should be complete, and I update it every month.

item.title: New Nintendo Switch 2 Game Is Being Review Bombed
item.description:
The newly re-released Pikmin 4 on the Switch 2 is being review-bombed, with players criticizing several aspects of its paid upgrade despite the original game's positive reception. Released in 2023, Pikmin 4 was among Nintendo's most acclaimed Switch exclusives, but its recently launched Switch 2 Edition is proving far more divisive.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Originally released on July 21, 2023, Pikmin 4 marked the first new numbered installment in Nintendo's classic strategy series in a decade. The game received widespread praise for its colorful environments, accessible gameplay, and the introduction of Oatchi, an adorable canine companion who assists players throughout their adventure. On the original Switch, it currently holds an 87 Metascore and an 8.9 user score on Metacritic, reflecting its generally positive reception. Most recently, Nintendo released Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy on November 12, offering enhanced visuals and additional content for $9.99 to existing owners. However, the upgrade has quickly become a source of frustration for some longtime fans.

Pikmin 4 Just Proved Nintendo Switch 2 Upgrades Need More Than Better Graphics

Pikmin 4 shows how Switch 2 upgrades can justify themselves by adding meaningful new ways to play, not just sharper visuals.

By Amina Ayoud

Pikmin 4's Nintendo Switch 2 Edition Is Being Review Bombed

At the time of this writing, the Metacritic user reviews for Pikmin 4 's Switch 2 Edition have been overwhelmingly negative, with the game receiving a user score of just 1.9 out of 10 from 306 ratings. This stands in sharp contrast to the original game's 8.9 user score, as well as the new edition's considerably more positive 83 Metascore from professional reviewers. Many negative fan reviews appear to question the value of the upgrade, with some players accusing Nintendo of making the game worse. One user, Kevosan, gave the release a 0/10 rating, stating the upgrade "actively makes the game worse" and criticized its performance and additional content.

Much of the current backlash centers on the Switch 2 Edition's technical shortcomings, which seem to make this release arguably worse than Pikmin 4 on the original Nintendo Switch. Although the upgrade introduces native 4K resolution when docked, the game remains limited to 30 FPS and also lacks support for the console's Joy-Con 2 mouse controls, which many fans expected would come naturally to a strategy game. More concerning are reports of longer loading times, with some players claiming that transitions between areas take significantly longer than on the original Switch. One user review claimed that certain loading screens had increased from approximately six seconds to more than 30 seconds, although the severity of these issues appears to vary between players.

Two iconic game characters. One impossible mashup.
Can you name them both?

Additionally, Pikmin 4 's new Dandori Academy mode has also attracted criticism, particularly regarding how its content is being distributed. Nintendo has promised 72 challenge stages for Pikmin 4 , but is releasing only six each month, meaning players cannot immediately access the full experience. Some fans have also criticized the mode for reusing environments and layouts from the original game rather than introducing entirely new locations. Beyond Dandori Academy, the upgrade adds voice commands for Oatchi and GameShare support for multiplayer Dandori Battles; however, these additions have done little to satisfy players who were primarily hoping for more substantial performance improvements in Pikmin 4 .

Despite the overwhelmingly negative user ratings, professional reviews of Pikmin 4 's Switch 2 Edition have been considerably more favorable. Many outlets have praised the improved visuals, Dandori Academy's potential, and the relatively inexpensive upgrade price, particularly for newcomers experiencing Pikmin 4 for the first time. Some fans have also argued that the extremely low Metacritic ratings are excessive, given that the original game remains largely unchanged. Whether Nintendo addresses the reported performance issues remains to be seen, but the backlash demonstrates how even a well-received game can face criticism when its paid upgrade fails to meet expectations.
